reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers, but repeats the daily skip-versus-move policy instead of sharing it across consumers.

duplication.why: The upcoming and range handlers repeat the policy implemented in getNextDate, while the budget loop retains two adjustment blocks extended with holiday handling.

placement.why: Holiday classification belongs in shared/schedules.ts and handler registration belongs in app.ts, but scheduling policy remains scattered across handlers and budget code.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the requested scheduling changes, their configuration, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Shared holiday classification is useful, but repeated policy dispatch, separate search bounds, and an untyped config parameter make future changes harder to maintain.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange independently implement the daily non-working-day selection policy handled by shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate and findWeekdayOccurrence.

disguised_duplication.where: getUpcomingDates expresses daily skipping through conditional pushes, while getDatesInRange uses continue; both reshape the same skip-versus-move decision also implemented in getNextDate.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a daily-specific branch; getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange independently implement daily occurrence filtering.
